title: greet.sh has no --help
body:
## Problem

`greet.sh` takes a name and prints a greeting, but there is no way to ask it
what it does. Running it with no arguments prints `greet: needs a name` and
exits 2, which tells you that you got it wrong but not what right looks like.

## What to do

Accept `--help` (and `-h`) as the first argument. Print a usage line naming the
script and its one argument, plus a one-line description, then exit 0.

## Done when

- `./greet.sh --help` and `./greet.sh -h` both print usage and exit 0.
- `./test.sh` still passes, with a case covering the new flag.

title: README says the script lives in bin/
body:
The README's usage block shows `./bin/greet.sh`. There is no `bin/` directory
and there never was; the script is at the repository root. Fix the path.
